package_info.package_name: N/A (GitHub repository manipulation, not a specific package)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire repository is considered malicious due to deliberate manipulation of commit metadata, including falsifying commit timestamps and author identities. This creates a deceptive history that falsely implies long-term, reputable contributions from trusted users, increasing the likelihood that developers will trust and use code from an attacker-controlled source.

execution_context.file_location: local git environment (before pushing to GitHub)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
set git GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2010-04-19 17:18:43
set git GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2010-04-19 17:18:43
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At commit-time, the code sets the GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE environment variables, causing git to record a falsified commit timestamp, resulting in repository history that displays fabricated historical activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it intentionally alters the commit timestamp to a date far in the past, which can make a repository appear older and more established than it actually is, misleading users about the project's credibility.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal commits should accurately reflect the time of contribution; falsifying timestamps undermines the integrity and trustworthiness of the repository's history.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, developers may backdate commits for migration or archival purposes, but systematic or bulk backdating is not standard practice and is highly unusual.
key_indicators: Commits with timestamps predating the creation of the repository or user account
Bulk commits with identical or patterned backdated timestamps
Unusual clustering of commit dates in the distant past

execution_context.file_location: local git environment (before pushing to GitHub)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
git config user.name <spoofed_username>
git config user.email <spoofed_email>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At commit-time, the code sets the git user.name and user.email configuration to impersonate another GitHub user, causing subsequent commits to be attributed to a trusted third party in the repository history.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Impersonating another user's identity in commit metadata is a clear attempt to mislead others about the true origin of code contributions, potentially leveraging the reputation of well-known developers to gain trust.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Commits should accurately reflect the true author; spoofing the author and email fields is deceptive and undermines the provenance and accountability of code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Occasionally, organizations may use generic or shared accounts for commits, but impersonating specific, unrelated users is not legitimate and is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
key_indicators: Commits attributed to well-known users who are not actual contributors to the repository
Mismatch between commit signature and displayed author identity
Sudden appearance of high-profile contributors without corresponding public activity

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Commits should reflect accurate authorship and timing; this process intentionally subverts those expectations by embedding false information into the repository.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While the git commit command is standard, its use in conjunction with spoofed metadata is not legitimate and is a strong indicator of malicious manipulation.
key_indicators: Commits with unverifiable or mismatched author and timestamp metadata
Commits lacking cryptographic signatures from the displayed author
Commit histories with patterns of spoofed or inconsistent metadata

behavioral_signatures: Commits with timestamps predating the creation date of the repository or user account
Commits attributed to well-known users who are not actual contributors to the project
Repositories exhibiting sudden, high-volume historical activity or backdated commit bursts
file_indicators: Bulk commits with identical or patterned commit messages
Commits lacking cryptographic signatures from the displayed author
Commit metadata with mismatched or unverifiable author information
network_indicators: N/A (no direct network activity in the manipulation process, but may correlate with scraping of public commit data for identity harvesting)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for commits with timestamps that are inconsistent with repository or user creation dates. Flag repositories with contributors whose commits are unsigned or whose commit signatures do not match the displayed author. Detect sudden spikes in historical activity or the appearance of high-profile contributors without corresponding public activity. Encourage and enforce the use of signed commits and enable vigilant mode to highlight unverified or spoofed contributions. Cross-reference commit metadata with known contributor lists to identify impersonation.
